full_judgment:
14. In reply, Dr. Kamal Hossain has argued on the maintainability of the writ petition and has submitted that the writ petition has not been filed for vindicating any of the terms and conditions of service of the petitioner. Conceding that the supersession of the petitioner has given rise to the present cause of action and has made him aggrieved the petitioner has challenged contravention of the Constitution by the Executive Organ of the State and, as such, this writ petition cannot be considered as a dispute relating to the terms and conditions of service of the petitioner. According to Dr. Hossain, by deliberately omitting to consult the Supreme Court as required by Article 116 of the Constitution before promoting and appointing several persons in the Judicial Service as Joint Secretaries, the Executive Organ acted arbitrarily. In further elaborating Dr. Hossain has emphasised that when it is palpable that the constitutional requirement of consultation was not fulfilled by the President before appointing three District Judges who were persons in the judicial service as Joint Secretaries in the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, the Executive Organ acted arbitrarily, because, non-compliance with the specific mandatory requirement of the Constitution before exercising the power vested by the Constitution itself involves arbitrariness in the exercise of the power so vested and when arbitrariness in exercising power is established and if by such arbitrariness any person is adversely affected there is clear violation of the equality clauses as enshrined in Article 27 of the Constitution in the general sense and also Article 29 of the Constitution in the limited sense when the violation complained of is in respect of opportunity of employment or office in the service of the Republic. As such, Dr. Hossain has submitted this writ petition is fundamentally an application for enforcement of Article 27 and Article 29 of the Constitution and Article 117 of the Constitution is not attracted and cannot stand as a bar against entertainment of this application by this Court. 

 27. The words,.............the power of posting promotion" occurring in Article 116 and the following words, " of persons employed in the judicial service and magistrates exercising judicial functions shall vest in the President and shall be exercised by him in consultation with the Supreme Court," clearly mean that whenever the question of posting or promoting a person employed in the judicial service and magistrates exercising judicial functions comes up for consideration before the President, consultation with the Supreme Court by the President is mandatory. The words, "posting, promotion" in this Article are not qualified by any other words and are left wide enough to include all sorts of posting and promotion of "persons employed in the judicial service". It is not disputed that posting and promotion of persons in the judicial service may also be in a non-judicial post. This is also clear from the impugned notification which says that the three District Judges belonging to the BCS. (Judicial) cadre were "on promotion" appointed as Joint Secretaries, etc. The words in the Article simply mean "posting, promotion" of whatever kind they may be whether from one judicial post to another judicial post or from a judicial post to a non-judicial post, "of persons employed in the judicial service" i.e. of all persons belonging to the judicial service. These words cannot be construed to mean "posting, promotion" in the judicial service" alone but of persons" belonging to the judicial service and the words, "posting promotion" being unqualified by any other word and "posting, promotion" of persons belonging to the judicial service may be admittedly made to a non-judicial post, as in the present case, these words must also mean posting and promotion to any non-judicial post as well. As such, it appears to us that not only when a person employed in the judicial service is promoted and/or posted to another post in the judicial service, but also when such person is promoted and/or posted to a post outside the judicial service, there is no scope from complying with the requirements of Article 116 of the Constitution. 

 63. Mr. Khan has also argued that this writ petition is badly defective for nonjoinder of M/s Aminullah, Khondakar Md. Abu Bakar and Md. Hasan Amin as they will be seriously affected if the Rule is made absolute. 

 65. Mr. Khan has argued that since the aforesaid prayer of the petitioner in that case was not allowed on the ground that the promoted persons were not made parties, so on the analogy of the said case this writ petition should be considered to be defective for nonjoinder of M/s Aminullah, Khondakar Md. Abu Bakar and Md. Hasan Amin who are likely to be affected if the prayer of the petitioner in this writ petition is allowed. 

 66. We have already said that innumerable persons had been promoted in that case and innumerable persons had no notice of that case but in the present case, all the three persons who were promoted by the impugned acts of the respondents are officers attached to this Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs and it appears from the record that the respondent No. 2 in this case who filed the affidavit-in-opposition is the Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs. It can, therefore, be presumed that the above three officers who are Joint Secretaries in the said Ministry are aware of this writ petition. In such circumstances, if they felt that they would be adversely affected by any decision taken by this Court they could have appeared before the Court and made their respective submissions. It cannot be conceived that three Joint Secretaries of the same Ministry from which the Secretary is contesting this writ petition are not aware of the subject-matter of this writ petition. Be that as it may, since it appears that the petitioner has impugned certain actions of the respondents and has claimed enforcement of his fundaments rights alleging infringement of such rights by the respondents and not by the aforesaid three persons, we are of opinion that this writ petition will not fail for their non-joinder. In this respect, we are tempted to quote an observation of the learned Appellate Division in Mr. Moudud Ahmed, Respondent petitioner vs. Mr. Anwar Hossain Khan, Advocate and others, Respondents 15 BLD 1995 (AD) 12. 

 68. We are unable to agree with Mr. Khan. The impugned acts were tainted with arbitrariness and the arbitrariness occurred for non-compliance with the mandatory provision of Article 116 of the Constitution requiring the President to consult with the Supreme Court as to the suitability or otherwise of persons in the judicial service eligible for promotion to the aforesaid posts. Even if the case of the petitioner was considered by the President, for omission to consult the Supreme Court before such consideration opened the possibility of an arbitrary decision and even if the bare possibility of an arbitrary decision is found to have been present, the ultimate action following such decision is bound to be held to be in contravention of the equality clauses guaranteed in Article 27 and Article 29 of the Constitution. Again, we are not unmindful of the fact that seniority alone cannot be the sole criterion for promotion. But, in this case the petitioner has not claimed promotion on the basis of his seniority. He has, on the contrary, challenged his exclusion in an arbitrary manner and by ignoring the constitutional requirements. We do not, therefore, find substance in Mr. Khan's contention.
